sections.title: Remote Sensing
sections.description: This course will introduce students to the principles of remote sensing, characteristics of remote sensors, and remote sensing applications. Image acquisition, data collection in the electromagnetic spectrum, and data set manipulations for earth and environmental science applications will be emphasized. We will cover fundamental knowledge of the physics of remote sensing; aerial photographic techniques; multispectral, hyperperspectral, thermal, and other image analysis. Students will pursue an independent research project using remote sensing tools, and at the end of the semester should have a good understanding and the basic skills of remote sensing.

sections.title: Remote Sensing (A)
sections.description:
Introduction to Remote Sensing introduces students to the principles of remote sensing, characteristics of remote sensors, and applications of remote sensing in the Earth and environmental sciences. Image acquisition, data collection across the electromagnetic spectrum, and analysis of remotely sensed data using Google Earth Engine will be emphasized. Topics include the physics of remote sensing; aerial photography; multispectral, hyperspectral, and thermal imagery; image interpretation; and spatial analysis. By the end of the course, students will understand how remotely sensed images are created, processed, analyzed, and applied to investigate environmental questions and challenges.
This is a Structured Active In-Class Learning course. Students build foundational knowledge outside of class through readings, videos, and practice exercises. Class time is devoted primarily to collaborative workshops in which students apply concepts and techniques using Google Earth Engine to analyze real-world environmental data and solve authentic problems.
This is also an Academically-Based Community Service (ABCS) course and integrates research, learning, and service. Working in teams, students partner with community organizations, schools, agencies, or other stakeholders to identify an environmental question, challenge, or information need that can be addressed using remote sensing. Through these projects, students experience remote sensing as a tool for community-engaged scholarship, bringing together academic knowledge and community expertise through collaborative, mutually beneficial partnerships. Students will apply remote sensing methods to generate information that helps communities better understand environmental conditions, evaluate potential solutions, and support decision-making.
In addition to developing technical skills in remote sensing and geospatial analysis, students will learn how scientific inquiry can contribute to the public good, strengthen relationships between universities and communities, and support democratic participation in addressing environmental challenges. The course emphasizes collaboration, reflection, ethical engagement, and the responsible use of Earth observation data to improve both community outcomes and student learning.
